title: Wake Up
summary: You doze off on the train home after a long day and wake somewhere wrong: a silent car of motionless passengers, black windows, stops you've never heard of, and a phone stuck at 2:14. An old woman across the aisle is horrified to see you, introduces herself as June and gives you a handwritten list of nine rules. The passengers copy your movements until you freeze; a man in a red tracksuit laughs it off; the conductor punches your ticket. June's own ticket has been punched hundreds of times.

lines.spoken: You finally get on the train after a long day. All you want is takeout and your bed.
lines.caption: after a **long day**

lines.spoken: The second you sit down, the fatigue hits. Four more stops. A small nap couldn't hurt.
lines.caption: a small **nap**

lines.spoken: If only you knew how wrong you'd be.
lines.caption: how **wrong** you'd be

lines.spoken: You wake up to silence. Just the clack of the tracks.
lines.caption: the **clack** of the tracks

lines.spoken: The car is full, but nobody moves. Every passenger hides behind a newspaper.
lines.caption: **nobody moves**

lines.spoken: Your phone says two fourteen in the morning. No signal.
lines.caption: **2:14**. **no signal**

lines.spoken: Outside the windows, nothing. Just black.
lines.caption: **just black**

lines.spoken: The route map above the doors lists stops you've never heard of.
lines.caption: stops you've **never heard of**

lines.spoken: Across the aisle, an old woman knits a red scarf so long it trails across the floor.
lines.caption: an **old woman** knits

lines.spoken: She's the only one not reading. She's watching you.
lines.caption: she's **watching** you

lines.spoken: When your eyes meet, her needles stop. Her face falls.
lines.caption: her **needles stop**

lines.spoken: "Oh no," she whispers. "Not another one."
lines.caption: **not another one**

lines.spoken: "Where are we?" you ask.
lines.caption: **where** are we

lines.spoken: "I'm so sorry, sweetheart," she says. "I'm June. Listen to me very carefully."
lines.caption: I'm **June**

lines.spoken: She presses a folded sheet of paper into your hands.
lines.caption: a **folded sheet**

lines.spoken: "Read it," June says. "And do exactly what it says."
lines.caption: do **exactly** what it says

lines.spoken: Rule one. Do not make eye contact with the other passengers.
lines.caption: do not make **eye contact**

lines.spoken: Rule two. When the conductor asks for your ticket, smile. Do not speak.
lines.caption: **smile**. do not **speak**

lines.spoken: Rule three. If the lights go out, keep your eyes closed until the doors chime.
lines.caption: keep your **eyes closed**

lines.spoken: Rule four. Never go into the last car.
lines.caption: never the **last car**

lines.spoken: Rule five. If someone calls your name, it isn't them.
lines.caption: it **isn't them**

lines.spoken: Rule six. Your stop is the one that shows your name on the map. Get off, no matter what is on the platform.
lines.caption: your **name** on the **map**

lines.spoken: Rule seven. Do not fall asleep again.
lines.caption: do not fall **asleep again**

lines.spoken: Rule eight. If your reflection blinks before you do, look away.
lines.caption: your **reflection** blinks

lines.spoken: Rule nine. If the passengers start copying you, freeze.
lines.caption: **freeze**

lines.spoken: You look up. Every newspaper is down. Every passenger is staring at you.
lines.caption: every passenger is **staring**

lines.spoken: You lift a hand to rub your eyes. Every hand in the car lifts too.
lines.caption: every hand **lifts**

lines.spoken: Rule nine. You freeze.
lines.caption: you **freeze**

lines.spoken: Then the newspapers rustle back up, all at once.
lines.caption: the newspapers **rustle** back

lines.spoken: Two rows down, a man in a red tracksuit laughs. "This is a prank show, right?"
lines.caption: a **red tracksuit**

lines.spoken: He yanks at the doors. They don't budge.
lines.caption: they don't **budge**

lines.spoken: Then, from the end of the car: click. Click.
lines.caption: **click**. **click**.

lines.spoken: A very tall conductor is coming down the aisle, punching tickets. His cap hides his eyes, but not his smile.
lines.caption: not his **smile**

lines.spoken: He stops at your seat. "Ticket, please."
lines.caption: **ticket**, please

lines.spoken: There's a ticket in your pocket you don't remember buying.
lines.caption: a **ticket** in your **pocket**

lines.spoken: Rule two. You smile and say nothing.
lines.caption: you **smile**

lines.spoken: Click. He punches it and moves on.
lines.caption: he **punches** it

lines.spoken: June stares at the hole. The color drains from her face.
lines.caption: the color **drains**

lines.spoken: She holds up her own ticket. It's punched so many times it looks like lace.
lines.caption: it looks like **lace**

lines.spoken: "One hole," she whispers, "for every stop you miss."
lines.caption: every **stop** you miss

lines.spoken: Your ticket has one hole.
lines.caption: **one hole**

lines.spoken: Hers has hundreds.
lines.caption: **hundreds**

shots.frame: train at night, you board tired

shots.action: hold, the clack of the tracks
push in on the strange stops
the old woman knitting, scarf across the floor
the needles stop; her face falls
every newspaper down, every face on you
tall, cap over his eyes, smiling

end_card.title: PART 2
end_card.hook: How long has June been riding?

continuity_out: Night 1, still 2:14 AM. You hold the rules sheet (nine rules, neat small handwriting you haven't recognised yet) and a ticket with one hole that was in your pocket. June has introduced herself; her ticket is punched hundreds of times. The man in the red tracksuit thinks it's a prank and keeps trying the doors. The passengers copy you when you move. The conductor has moved on toward the last car. Nobody has said the next stop yet.
